# Parity Fixtures

These 6 JSON files are the **parity pins** for the PRIMORDIA native (Godot/GDScript)
port of the TypeScript simulation core. They were generated by running the frozen
TypeScript source (`/home/misa/Desktop/RD/Spore`, the reference implementation).
Every port test that reimplements a piece of the sim compares its output against
these files — **exactness matters more than elegance**. Floats are written at full
IEEE-754 double precision (what `JSON.stringify` produces); a port passes only when
its doubles match bit-for-bit, not within an epsilon.

- Source of truth: TS modules under `src/` in the Spore repo
- Generator: `~/Desktop/RD/Spore/tools/fixture-gen.test.ts` (uncommitted tool, the
  TS repo is frozen; it modifies no game source)
- Regeneration: see bottom of this file

---

## rng_stream.json

Deterministic fingerprint of the `Rng` class (Mulberry32, `src/core/rng.ts`).

```json
{
  "seedOrder": [1, 42, 3735928559],
  "consumptionOrder": ["next x50", "int(2,8) x20", "chance(0.3) x20",
                       "weighted([[1,\"a\"],[3,\"b\"],[0.5,\"c\"]]) x10",
                       "gauss() x10", "branch() x3 -> child seed (child.state())"],
  "streams": [
    {
      "seed": 1,
      "next":        [50 floats],        // r.next()
      "int_2_8":     [20 ints],          // r.int(2, 8)   — inclusive
      "chance_0_3":  [20 booleans],      // r.chance(0.3) — next() < 0.3
      "weighted":    [10 strings],       // r.weighted([[1,"a"],[3,"b"],[0.5,"c"]])
      "gauss":       [10 floats],        // r.gauss() — Irwin-Hall, mean 0 sd 1
      "branch_seeds":[3 ints]            // child.state() after each r.branch()
    },
    ...
  ]
}
```

Each stream uses ONE fresh `Rng(seed)`, consumed in exactly the order listed in
`consumptionOrder` (state carries across the sections). `3735928559` is 0xDEADBEEF.
`branch()` draws one parent value; the recorded number is the child's internal
state — i.e. the seed a port must reproduce for the child stream.

## genome_stats.json

`computeCellStats` + `computeCreatureStats` (`src/evo/stats.ts`) for 8 fixed genomes.

```json
{
  "keyNote": "key = genomeHash(genome)",
  "genomes": {
    "<genomeHash>": { "name": "...", "genome": {...}, "cell": {...}, "creature": {...} }
  }
}
```

Key is `genomeHash(genome)` (`src/evo/genome.ts`) — the dash-joined fingerprint
used for bestiary dedup; the 8 hashes are distinct. Stats are pure math over the
genome; note that `diet` never affects stats (the three diet variants have
identical stat blocks but different hashes).

Genome recipes (all built from `defaultGenome()` + overrides; `generation` is 1
unless stated):

| name | overrides |
|---|---|
| `default` | none |
| `all-min` | size 0.6, diet herbivore, hue 0, sat 0.05, every numeric gene at its `GENE_BOUNDS` min (flagella/cilia/spikes/jaw/toxin/proboscis/electro/jet/legs/arms/horns/wings/brain all 0, eyes 1 — its bound min is 1), tail false, coat skin, pattern plain |
| `all-max` | size 2.2, diet carnivore, hue 240, sat 1, pattern stripes, flagella 6, cilia 4, spikes 8, jaw 5, toxin 5, proboscis 3, electro 3, jet 3, legs 8, arms 4, eyes 6, horns 4, tail true, wings 2, brain 5, coat plates, generation 9 |
| `legless-2.2` | size 2.2, flagella 4, jet 2, jaw 3, legs 0 — pins the legless-worm speed exemption (`legs === 0` skips the size penalty) |
| `glow-fur` | pattern glow, coat fur, eyes 4, arms 2, brain 1, wings 1 — exercises every charm bonus branch |
| `herbivore-variant` | shared body (below) + diet herbivore |
| `carnivore-variant` | shared body + diet carnivore |
| `omnivore-variant` | shared body + diet omnivore |

Shared body for the diet variants: size 1.4, hue 200, sat 0.7, pattern spots,
flagella 3, cilia 1, spikes 2, jaw 2, toxin 1, proboscis 0, electro 0, jet 1,
legs 4, arms 2, eyes 3, horns 1, tail true, wings 0, brain 2, coat scales,
generation 3.

## eco_tick.json

One 10-minute `Ecosystem` simulation (`src/evo/ecosystem.ts`), no world-trait mods.

```json
{
  "ecoSeed": 7,                        // Ecosystem(new Rng(7)) — names, ids, speciation
  "dt": 1, "ticks": 600, "snapshotEvery": 60,
  "roster": [ { "genome": {...}, "pop": 9 }, ... ],   // added in this order
  "snapshots": [
    { "t": 0, "flora": 60.0, "totalEaten": 0,
      "species": [ { "id": "sp0_6pfqjc", "name": "Glorurp Leaflover",
                     "pop": 9.0, "extinct": false }, ... ] },
    ...  // t = 0, 60, 120, ..., 600 → 11 snapshots
  ]
}
```

Roster (hand-built from `defaultGenome()` + overrides, in add order; pops 4..9):

1. pop 9 — size 0.7, herbivore, flagella 3, eyes 2
2. pop 7 — size 1.8, herbivore, flagella 1, spikes 1
3. pop 8 — size 1.2, omnivore, jaw 2, flagella 2
4. pop 5 — size 0.9, carnivore, jaw 3, spikes 2, flagella 4
5. pop 4 — size 2.0, carnivore, jaw 4, spikes 3, flagella 2
6. pop 6 — size 0.6, omnivore, flagella 5, proboscis 1

`t = 0` is snapshot **before** the first tick; then `tick(1)` runs 600 times and a
snapshot lands every time `t % 60 === 0`. `pop` is a float after the first tick.
No `notifyKill` calls (`totalEaten` stays 0), no species goes extinct in this
walk (`extinct` stays false), no speciation fired — the pin is the exact
population/flora trajectory, including the flora floor (12) being reached.

## mutate_crossover.json

Mutation operators (`src/evo/mutation.ts`).

```json
{
  "parents": { "a": {...}, "b": {...} },   // the two fixed parent genomes
  "mutates":            [ { "i": 0, "rate": 0.35, "rngSeed": 0, "base": "defaultGenome()",
                            "genome": {...}, "hash": "..." }, ... 20 ],
  "crossovers":         [ { "j": 0, "rngSeed": 100, "mutateRate": 0.18,
                            "genome": {...}, "hash": "..." }, ... 10 ],
  "biasedCrossovers":   [ { "j": 0, "rngSeed": 200, "mutateRate": 0.18,
                            "bias": { "rate_add": 0.15, "dietPull": "carnivore" },
                            "genome": {...}, "hash": "..." }, ... 5 ]
}
```

- `mutates[i]` = `mutate(defaultGenome(), new Rng(i), 0.35)`, i = 0..19
- `crossovers[j]` = `crossover(A, B, new Rng(100 + j))`, j = 0..9 (default mutate rate 0.18, no opts)
- `biasedCrossovers[j]` = `crossover(A, B, new Rng(200 + j), 0.18, { bias: { rate_add: 0.15, dietPull: "carnivore" } })`, j = 0..4

Parent recipes (from `defaultGenome()` + overrides):

- **A**: size 1.6, diet herbivore, hue 80, sat 0.6, pattern spots, flagella 3,
  spikes 4, jaw 0, eyes 2, legs 5, tail true, coat fur, generation 4
- **B**: size 0.8, diet carnivore, hue 320, sat 0.4, pattern stripes, flagella 1,
  spikes 1, jaw 5, toxin 2, electro 1, jet 1, eyes 4, arms 1, legs 2, wings 1,
  brain 1, coat scales, generation 7

## world_genome.json

World-genome derivation and the reveal/turn/combo pump (`src/evo/worldGenome.ts`).

```json
{
  "seeds": [ { "seed": 0, "traitIds": [...], "temperament": "none|cradle|lean|wildcard",
               "turnIds": [...] }, ... ],          // deriveWorldGenome(seed), seeds 0..19
  "walks": {
    "seed0": { "steps": [...], "final": {...} },
    "seed2": { "steps": [...], "final": {...} }
  }
}
```

`seeds` is the plain derive table for seeds 0..19: `traitIds` in draw order,
`temperament`, and `turnIds` (the 0-2 world turns assigned at derive).

Each walk step is ONE `tickWorldReveals(world, signals)` call on a FRESH
`deriveWorldGenome(seed)`; state (revealed/comboFired/traits) carries across steps.
Per step: `step` (0-based), `why` (intent), `signals`
(`{stage, timer, chaos, kills, extinctions}`), `revealed` (ids newly revealed this
call), `combos` (ids fired this call), `turn` (turn id or null). `final` carries the
end state: `traitIds`, `temperament`, `revealed`, `comboFired`, `firedTurns`.

**seed0 walk** (derived traits: old_blood, mutation_moon, hungry_bloom, iron_gut;
no turns; temperament none) — pins all five reveal-condition kinds and boundaries:

| step | stage | timer | chaos | kills | ext | expected |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | cell | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | nothing |
| 1 | cell | 89 | 0 | 0 | 0 | nothing (just under) |
| 2 | cell | 90 | 0 | 0 | 0 | reveal hungry_bloom |
| 3 | cell | 179 | 0 | 0 | 0 | nothing |
| 4 | cell | 180 | 0 | 0 | 0 | reveal old_blood |
| 5 | cell | 200 | 0 | 14 | 0 | nothing (kills just under) |
| 6 | cell | 200 | 0 | 15 | 0 | reveal iron_gut |
| 7 | cell | 200 | 0.44 | 15 | 0 | nothing |
| 8 | cell | 200 | 0.59 | 15 | 0 | nothing (chaos just under) |
| 9 | cell | 200 | 0.61 | 15 | 0 | reveal mutation_moon |
| 10 | creature | 0 | 0.61 | 15 | 0 | nothing (no stageEnter trait) |
| 11 | creature | 100 | 0.61 | 15 | 0 | nothing |
| 12 | tribe | 0 | 0.61 | 15 | 0 | nothing |
| 13 | tribe | 60 | 0.61 | 15 | 0 | nothing (war_graves pair incomplete) |
| 14 | civ | 0 | 0.61 | 15 | 0 | nothing |
| 15 | cell | 220 | 0.61 | 15 | 1 | nothing (rot_circle needs toxin_sea; no turns derived) |
| 16 | space | 0 | 0.61 | 15 | 1 | nothing |

**seed2 walk** (derived traits: pirate_wind, mutation_moon, hungry_bloom,
toxin_sea, kin_memory, world_temperament; temperament cradle) — pins combo firing:

| step | stage | timer | chaos | kills | ext | expected |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | cell | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | nothing |
| 1 | cell | 90 | 0 | 0 | 0 | reveal hungry_bloom |
| 2 | cell | 91 | 0 | 0 | 0 | nothing |
| 3 | cell | 250 | 0 | 0 | 0 | nothing |
| 4 | cell | 300 | 0 | 0 | 0 | reveal world_temperament |
| 5 | cell | 300 | 0.44 | 0 | 0 | nothing |
| 6 | cell | 300 | 0.45 | 0 | 0 | reveal toxin_sea — `above` is inclusive (`>= 0.45`) |
| 7 | cell | 300 | 0.46 | 0 | 0 | nothing (toxin_sea already revealed) |
| 8 | cell | 300 | 0.46 | 1 | 0 | reveal kin_memory |
| 9 | cell | 300 | 0.59 | 1 | 0 | nothing |
| 10 | cell | 300 | 0.61 | 1 | 0 | reveal mutation_moon; fire selection_sweep |
| 11 | cell | 300 | 0.61 | 5 | 1 | fire rot_circle |
| 12 | cell | 300 | 0.7 | 10 | 2 | nothing (both combos already fired) |
| 13 | tribe | 0 | 0.7 | 10 | 2 | reveal pirate_wind (stageEnter) |
| 14 | space | 0 | 0.7 | 10 | 2 | nothing |

Note step 10: within one `tickWorldReveals` call the reveal loop runs first, then
the combo loop — so a trait revealed this tick can complete a combo the same tick.

## storyteller_walk.json

Storyteller mood timeline (`src/game/storyteller.ts`): one fresh `Storyteller()`
(mood `test`, temperament `none`), `update(1, signals)` × 120 ticks.

```json
{
  "dt": 1, "ticks": 120,
  "phases": [ { "name": "struggling", "ticks": 30, "signals": {...} }, ... ],
  "timeline": [ { "t": 1, "phase": "struggling",
                  "signals": { "chaos": 0.2, "ecoHealth": 0.2, "karma": 0,
                               "dnaRate": 5, "deathsInStage": 3, "stageTime": 1 },
                  "mood": "bless", "hold": 20.0 }, ... ]
}
```

Signal script — four 30-tick phases in order; `stageTime = t` (advances 1/tick):

| phase | ticks | chaos | ecoHealth | karma | dnaRate | deathsInStage | expected mood driver |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| struggling | 1–30 | 0.2 | 0.2 | 0 | 5 | 3 | bless (ecoHealth < 0.35, deaths ≥ 2) |
| neutral | 31–60 | 0.3 | 0.8 | 0.1 | 10 | 0 | test |
| aggressive-dominant | 61–90 | 0.8 | 0.9 | −0.8 | 40 | 0 | twist (chaos > 0.55, dnaRate > 25) |
| pacifist-high-karma | 91–120 | 0.7 | 0.9 | 0.8 | 30 | 0 | test — pacifist gate (karma ≥ 0.5) blocks twist despite chaos/dnaRate |

`hold` is the hysteresis counter AFTER the update (MIN_HOLD = 20); because each
phase runs 30 > 20 ticks, the mood flips exactly at each phase boundary — the
fixture pins those boundary ticks. `noteChaosEvent` is never called (temperament
pacing is not exercised here).

## Regenerating

From the TS repo root (the generator needs its own vitest config because the
repo's frozen `vitest.config.ts` only includes `tests/**`):

```bash
cd ~/Desktop/RD/Spore && npx vitest run --config tools/vitest.config.ts tools/fixture-gen.test.ts
```

The generator asserts while writing: every number must be finite (NaN/Infinity
abort the run — they would otherwise reach the JSON as `null`), and every file is
parsed back and deep-compared against the data in memory. Do not hand-edit the
JSON: change the generator, regenerate, and re-document here.
